title: Database Sessions and Connections
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of database sessions and connections in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to database engines.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers database sessions and connections within database integration. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use database sessions and connections to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is data integrity, transaction boundaries, schema evolution and bounded database access.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Database Sessions and Connections matters because it is part of database integration. In practice, focus on data integrity, transaction boundaries, schema evolution and bounded database access. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Database engines
items.text: Apply database engines against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Database Sessions and Connections”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Database engines” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Database Sessions and Connections, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
